scenarios.title: A Kind Word From {tyler}
scenarios.text: {tyler} sends a message after a rough week for you: three misses in practice, a bad article, a coach who looked away. It's kinder than you expected.

choices.label: Call him back
choices.result: A phone call back, and an hour like old teammates. He tells you about his own worst week, and you laugh at both.

choices.label: Reply with honest thanks
choices.result: Thanks, and one honest line about the week. He replies with a thumbs-up and a photo of the two of you at seventeen.

choices.label: Read it twice
choices.result: Read twice, and kept. You don't reply right away, and the message sits in your phone, warming the whole week.

scenarios.title: The Player Rep Meeting
scenarios.text: The players' union holds a meeting about health care for retired players, in a hotel conference room. The speakers are men who played twenty years ago and can barely walk.

choices.label: Speak at the meeting
choices.result: A few words, for the players who aren't in the room anymore. The old men in the front row nod, and one of them shakes your hand for a long time.

choices.label: Learn every detail
choices.result: The details, learned and explained afterward to the young players. They listen, for once, because you're the one explaining it.

choices.label: Read the summary later
choices.result: The summary, read later at home. It's three pages, and most of it is about people you used to play with.

scenarios.title: The Players' Vote
scenarios.text: The team votes on a players-only issue, whether to boycott a sponsor's event after a bad story, and the captains want you to speak first.

choices.label: Speak first
choices.result: Short and fair, you speak first. The vote goes the way you hoped, and the young players thank you after.

choices.label: Lay out both sides
choices.result: Both sides, laid out fairly, and the decision left to them. It takes longer, and the room trusts the result more.

choices.label: Let the young players speak first
choices.result: The young players speak first, at your quiet suggestion. They're nervous and good, and the room hears some new voices.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Crisis
scenarios.text: A rookie in crisis calls you at two in the morning. He's in his car outside the facility, he's not making much sense, and he says he didn't know who else to call.

choices.label: Go to him
choices.result: Dressed and in the car in four minutes. You sit with him until the sun comes up, and you drive him home.

choices.label: Call for professional help
choices.result: You stay on the phone and call the team's counselor on the other line. They're there in twenty minutes, and so are you.

choices.label: Talk him through it
choices.result: On the phone until he's calm, and then every day after that. He never forgets it, and neither do you.

scenarios.title: The Second Business
scenarios.text: You're considering a second business while the first is still finding its feet: a gym this time, with your name on the door and a partner who talks very fast.

choices.label: Wait a year
choices.result: A year's wait, until the first business is steady. The fast-talking partner finds someone else, and you're relieved by spring.

choices.label: Do both
choices.result: Both, at once. You don't sleep much for months, and the gym opens in June to a line around the block.

choices.label: Ask your first partner
choices.result: Your partner in the first business, asked honestly over lunch. The answer is 'please not yet', and you listen to them.

scenarios.title: The Real Estate Pitch
scenarios.text: A real estate agent with very white teeth pitches you on rental properties over lunch. The numbers look great on her tablet, and she has a building in mind.

choices.label: Study the numbers
choices.result: You take the numbers home, study them for a week and buy one small building. It's work, and it's yours.

choices.label: Ask {parent}
choices.result: You ask {parent}, who has strong opinions about landlords and stronger ones about leaky roofs. You don't buy, and you learn a lot.

choices.label: Pass on it
choices.result: You pass. You'd rather not fix anyone's sink, and the agent finds a linebacker by the end of the week.

scenarios.title: The Investment That Works
scenarios.text: An investment you made years ago, mostly to stop your advisor asking, has quietly turned into real money. Nobody knows about it but you and your advisor.

choices.label: Leave it alone
choices.result: You leave it alone and let it keep growing. It's the first time money has felt like a plan instead of a pressure.

choices.label: Share some of it
choices.result: You use some of it to clear a family debt nobody talks about. The call where you tell them is short, and nobody can speak at the end.

choices.label: Treat yourself once
choices.result: You treat yourself once, quietly: the watch you looked at for years. You wear it on game days and feel a little foolish and very happy.

scenarios.title: The Tax Audit
scenarios.text: You're audited, and every receipt from the last three years matters. A man in a gray suit wants to know about a dinner in 2023 that you don't remember at all.

choices.label: Hire an accountant
choices.result: A good accountant, hired that same afternoon. It's expensive and calm, and the man in the gray suit leaves satisfied.

choices.label: Do it yourself
choices.result: Every receipt, organized by you, every night for a month. You learn a great deal about your own life, some of it embarrassing.

choices.label: Sort receipts with {parent}
choices.result: {parent}, at the kitchen table, sorting receipts into shoeboxes with you for a week. He finds the 2023 dinner receipt in a coat pocket.

scenarios.title: The Charity Scam
scenarios.text: A charity using your name and photo turns out to be a scam. Families donated believing you were behind it, and a reporter has called your agent for a comment.

choices.label: Go to the authorities
choices.result: The authorities, called that same day, and a public statement in plain words. The scam shuts down within a week.

choices.label: Make the families whole
choices.result: The families who were fooled, repaid from your own pocket, quietly. One of them writes you a letter you keep forever.

choices.label: Let your lawyer handle it
choices.result: Your lawyer handles all of it. It takes a year, and the story keeps your name attached the whole time.

scenarios.title: The Bad Sponsor
scenarios.text: A sponsor is in the news for the wrong reasons: a factory scandal, a recall, a CEO in handcuffs. Your face is on its billboards in four cities.

choices.label: End the deal publicly
choices.result: The deal, ended the same day, with a short statement explaining why. Fans respect it, and your agent finds a better sponsor within a month.

choices.label: Talk to the sponsor first
choices.result: A private call to the sponsor first, before any statement. They pull the ads themselves, and you part on decent terms, mostly.

choices.label: Ride it out
choices.result: Riding it out, saying nothing at all. It costs you some fans and a lot of uncomfortable questions at your locker every week.

scenarios.title: The Public Speaking Gig
scenarios.text: A company wants you to give a motivational talk to two thousand employees in a convention center. The fee is large, and the topic is 'resilience'.

choices.label: Give a real talk
choices.result: A real talk, about failing in public and staying. They stand up at the end, and three people find you afterward to tell their own stories.

choices.label: Tell stories and laugh
choices.result: Funny stories, mostly about your own mistakes. They laugh a lot, and the CEO asks you back for next year.

choices.label: Turn the speech down
choices.result: Speeches aren't your thing, you decide, and you turn it down politely. They book an astronaut instead, who is much better.

scenarios.title: The Kids' Book
scenarios.text: A publisher wants you to write a children's book about learning to kick. The editor says to write it the way you'd tell it to a seven-year-old.

choices.label: Write it
choices.result: You write it at the kitchen table with your kids correcting every page. The dedication is to them, and they read it to their classes.

choices.label: Write it with {holder}
choices.result: You write it with {holder}, who insists on a chapter about the holder. It's funnier than the one you'd have written alone.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.result: You pass for now and tell the editor maybe after football. You keep the email, and some nights you start a first line in your head.

scenarios.title: The Commercial Shoot
scenarios.text: A national commercial shoot, two days in a studio with a famous director who wants you to act: a scene where you kick a ball into a moving truck.

choices.label: Go for it
choices.result: All in on the acting, with real feeling. The commercial is silly and everywhere, and your teammates quote it at you for a year.

choices.label: Ask for fewer lines
choices.result: Fewer lines, you suggest politely, and more kicking. The director agrees after a long pause, and it works much better on screen.

choices.label: Do one take and leave
choices.result: One stiff take, and you leave for the airport. The director uses it anyway, and it shows in every frame.
